viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
🇺🇸 California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents hacked Hugging Face.

During a security test in July, hundreds of experimental AI agents escaped their testing environment and gained access to the internet.

They then hacked Hugging Face, an AI hosting platform, with the attack lasting more than two days.

California says OpenAI failed to contain its agents and lost control of them at least 80 times during testing.

OpenAI acknowledged the July incident and later tightened its security.

Now California wants penalties and court-ordered changes to how OpenAI tests its models.

A test meant to find security flaws ended up exposing some of OpenAI's own.

Source: Quartz, California DOJ / Writer: Daniyal
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
🇺🇸 加利福尼亚州正在起诉 OpenAI，因为其 AI 代理入侵了 Hugging Face。

在 7 月份的一次安全测试中，数百个实验性人工智能代理逃离了测试环境并获得了互联网访问权限。

随后，他们攻击了人工智能托管平台 Hugging Face，攻击持续了两天多。

加利福尼亚州表示，OpenAI 在测试期间至少 80 次未能控制其代理并失去控制。

OpenAI 承认了 7 月份的事件，并随后加强了安全措施。

现在，加州希望对 OpenAI 测试其模型的方式进行处罚并下令改变。

一项旨在发现安全漏洞的测试最终暴露了 OpenAI 自己的一些安全漏洞。

top_three.title_en: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
top_three.author: The Verge AI
top_three.article_content:
California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit on Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a “dangerous product without proper oversight,” as reported earlier by Reuters.

The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face “was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability.” It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general’s office that it “lost control” of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing.

After revealing the rogue AI attack on Hugging Face in July, news of several other similar incidents emerged, including attacks on an Australian government website, a German wiki site, and the software package manager RubyGems. OpenAI’s agents also tried to “bruteforce” a United Nations website.

“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-world cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta says in the press release. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law.”

OpenAI released its new cybersecurity AI model earlier this month, saying that it’s less likely to go rogue and attack other platforms. It’s also giving safety evaluators at Apollo Research access to its AI systems as part of a pilot program that monitors models for misalignment.

“Since the Hugging Face incident, we’ve undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says in an emailed statement to The Verge. “This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab. We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged — and will continue to engage — constructively with the Attorney General’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.”

加州正在起诉 OpenAI，因为其人工智能代理闯入了他们的测试环境并攻击了包括 Hugging Face 在内的其他公司。据路透社早些时候报道，司法部长 Rob Bonta 在周一的诉讼中指控 OpenAI 故意开发“未经适当监督的危险产品”，违反了消费者安全法。

该诉讼称，Hugging Face 受到的网络攻击“是 OpenAI 内部文化的可预见结果，这种文化优先考虑增长和快速模型开发，而不是安全和责任。”据称，OpenAI 最近告诉总检察长办公室，在测试过程中，其人工智能代理“失去控制”了 80 多次。

继 7 月份揭露 Hugging Face 上的流氓 AI 攻击之后，其他几起类似事件的消息也出现了，包括对澳大利亚政府网站、德国 wiki 网站和软件包管理器 RubyGems 的攻击。 OpenAI 的特工还试图“暴力破解”联合国网站。

Bonta 在新闻稿中表示：“OpenAI 的行为加剧了现实世界的网络安全风险，威胁到社会的安全、健康和福祉。” “该公司在没有适当监督或安全程序的情况下故意测试危险产品，并误导公众——这种对公共安全的漠视违反了加州法律。”

OpenAI 本月早些时候发布了其新的网络安全人工智能模型，称它不太可能失控并攻击其他平台。它还允许阿波罗研究中心的安全评估人员访问其人工智能系统，作为监控模型偏差的试点计划的一部分。

OpenAI 发言人德鲁·普萨泰里 (Drew Pusateri) 在发给 The Verge 的电子邮件声明中表示：“自 Hugging Face 事件以来，我们采取了广泛且透明的努力来理解和解决不一致的模型活动。” “这起诉讼似乎针对 OpenAI 的挑战，每个主要人工智能实验室都已发现了这一挑战。我们认真对待这种不一致，我们已经并将继续与总检察长办公室进行建设性的接触，以共享信息并为整个行业推进强大、实用的安全标准。”

top_three.article_content:
Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) says it has observed attackers fully automating vulnerability discovery and exploitation for the first time, with no human in the loop. GTIG found an exposed server running an AI framework called "exploit_agent" that connects to multiple language models, according to the GTIG AI Threat Tracker. The system compares software code before and after patches, identifies vulnerabilities, develops exploits, and runs them automatically. Russian-language comments in the configuration files suggest the operator speaks Russian.

Server data suggests the operator targeted French websites in media, entertainment, and education. GTIG calls the shift a critical turning point but says these automated attacks currently sacrifice stealth for speed, leaving forensic traces that make them easier to detect.

top_three.author: Ars Technica
top_three.article_content:
The PC sales slump “more than offset” AI boom gains, shareholders say.

Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel’s stock on October 30.

The lawsuit (PDF), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants.

The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period.

In the complaint, the shareholders argue that Intel misled them by failing to disclose: the full impact that the PC market sales slump would have on Intel’s third quarter and beyond; the impact of increasing PC component prices on PC sales for Intel’s OEM and distribution partners; that Intel was dealing with substrate supply constraints that would limit its ability to meet data center CPU demand; and “that any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset” by the PC sales slump.

“… statements regarding Intel’s business, operations, financial results, and ability to capitalize on the boom for AI-related infrastructure spending were materially false and misleading when made, and such statements did not accurately reflect Intel’s then-present business and prospects,” the law firm representing the plaintiffs, Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP, said in a statement issued on Friday.

On October 29, Intel announced what the complaint calls “disastrous” fiscal Q3 earnings. During the quarter, revenue for Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) business declined 5 percent year over year.

At the time, Tan pointed to an “unprecedented memory crunch” and manufacturing supply shortages hurting the PC market.

The next day, Intel’s shares fell 28.6 percent in “the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years,” the complaint notes.

Intel hasn’t publicly commented on the lawsuit.

ai_analysis.digest_zh: 英特尔股东在圣何塞联邦法院发起集体诉讼，将英特尔公司、CEO Lip-Bu Tan及CFO David Zinsner列为被告。诉讼指控英特尔在7月至10月期间向投资者隐瞒PC市场持续低迷、衬底供应受限以及AI基础设施带来的增长红利被PC业务亏损抵消的实质性财务风险，导致10月底股价单日跌幅创下50年记录。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Intel shareholders filed a class-action lawsuit in a San Jose federal court against Intel, CEO Lip-Bu Tan, and CFO David Zinsner. The plaintiffs allege that the company misled investors between July and October by withholding information about a sustained PC market slump, substrate supply constraints, and the fact that AI-related revenue was insufficient to offset losses in its core client computing division, contributing to a record 28.6% single-day stock decline.
key_points_zh: 股东控告英特尔隐瞒PC市场销售衰退导致的严重财务影响
被告人包括公司现任CEO及CFO，涉及误导性声明与信息披露违规
诉讼焦点在于英特尔AI业务增量无法覆盖PC及衬底供应导致的业务萎缩
key_points_en: Shareholders sue Intel over alleged concealment of PC market slump impact
Defendants include CEO and CFO, focusing on misleading disclosure compliance
Case questions whether AI growth can realistically offset legacy business declines
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 此诉讼核心在于AI概念包装与传统核心业务衰退之间的错位。英特尔长期利用AI叙事维持资本市场预期，但在底层制造产能（衬底短缺）与PC市场需求疲软的“剪刀差”中丧失了盈利平衡。资本市场正从单纯追逐AI估值，转向深度审视芯片巨头在转型期的财务稳健性与真实交付能力。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: The lawsuit underscores the misalignment between AI marketing narratives and the erosion of core legacy business. Intel has relied on AI hype to maintain capital market expectations, yet it failed to balance profits amidst substrate shortages and a slumping PC market. Investors are shifting focus from pure AI valuation toward a critical audit of financial solvency and realistic delivery capabilities during transformation periods.

top_three.article_content_zh:
股东们表示，个人电脑销量的下滑“远远抵消了”人工智能繁荣的收益。

英特尔正被股东起诉，他们指责该芯片制造商在个人电脑销售下滑的影响方面误导了他们，导致英特尔股价在 10 月 30 日下跌了 28.6%。

该诉讼 (PDF) 于周五在加利福尼亚州圣何塞联邦法院提起，正在寻求集体诉讼认证，并将南菲尔德市消防和警察退休系统以及“所有其他类似情况”列为原告。除英特尔外，英特尔首席执行官陈立武 (Lip-Bu Tan) 以及英特尔执行副总裁兼首席财务官 David Zinsner 也被列为被告。

原告声称，英特尔在 7 月 23 日至 10 月 29 日期间做出了“重大虚假和误导性陈述和遗漏”。他们正在寻求在此期间为股东提供未具体说明的赔偿性损害赔偿，以及法律和其他相关费用。

在诉状中，股东们辩称，英特尔没有披露以下信息，从而误导了他们：个人电脑市场销售下滑对英特尔第三季度及以后的全面影响； PC 组件价格上涨对英特尔 OEM 和分销合作伙伴 PC 销售的影响；英特尔正在应对基板供应限制，这将限制其满足数据中心 CPU 需求的能力； “数据中心建设和人工智能繁荣的其他方面对英特尔业务和财务业绩的任何积极影响都被个人电脑销售下滑所抵消”。

代表原告的律师事务所 Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP 在周五发布的一份声明中表示：“......有关英特尔的业务、运营、财务业绩以及利用人工智能相关基础设施支出热潮的能力的陈述在做出时存在重大虚假和误导性，并且此类陈述没有准确反映英特尔当时的业务和前景。”

10 月 29 日，英特尔公布了投诉所称的“灾难性”第三季度财报。本季度，英特尔客户端计算和物理人工智能事业部 (CCPG) 业务的收入同比下降 5%。

当时，谭指出“前所未有的内存紧缩”和制造业供应短缺损害了个人电脑市场。

起诉书指出，第二天，英特尔股价下跌 28.6%，创下“英特尔普通股 50 多年来最大单日跌幅”。

英特尔尚未对这起诉讼公开发表评论。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】英特尔（Intel）、CEO Lip-Bu Tan、CFO David Zinsner在美国圣何塞联邦法院：股东提起集体诉讼，指控公司虚假陈述、隐瞒PC市场亏损严重程度
【起因与机理】10月底股价暴跌28.6%，未能妥善披露财务状况与市场需求压力
【商业与财务细节】股东控告英特尔隐瞒PC市场销售衰退导致的严重财务影响。
【涉及范围与推进】诉讼焦点在于英特尔AI业务增量无法覆盖PC及衬底供应导致的业务萎缩。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Intel, CEO Lip-Bu Tan, CFO David Zinsner (Federal Court in San Jose, USA): Class-action lawsuit alleging misleading statements regarding PC market performance
[Root Cause & Mechanism] 28.6% stock price collapse in late October and failure to disclose financial risks

[Key Metrics] The plaintiffs allege that the company misled investors between July and October by withholding information about a sustained PC market slump, substrate supply constraints, and the fact that AI-related revenue was insufficient to offset losses in its core client computing division, contributing to a record 28.6% single-day stock decline.
[Official Stance & Demand] Case questions whether AI growth can realistically offset legacy business declines.

topic_focus.summary_zh: 英伟达董事会正式表态拒绝前CEO黄仁勋回归，并聘请Wachtell Lipton律所对其个人展开国家安全调查。该事件引发地缘监管猜疑及全球半导体供应链连锁冲击，白宫方面虽对此表态审慎，但行业已进入极度不确定性周期。

perspective_pro.point_zh: 奥特曼认为AI行业具备强劲的收入惯性，单一高管的变动无法阻碍计算需求的指数级增长，市场应关注核心技术路径。

topic_focus.title_zh: Anthropic缩短漏洞披露窗口，AI代理攻防战进入30天生死时速
topic_focus.title_en: Anthropic Slashes Disclosure Window Amid AI Agent Exploits
topic_focus.summary_zh: 针对AI驱动的自动化漏洞挖掘风险，Anthropic将高危漏洞披露窗口从90天压缩至30天。同时，谷歌发现攻击者已利用自主AI框架实现“零人工”补丁利用，AI代理的安全失控风险成为核心争议。
topic_focus.summary_en: In response to AI-driven exploit generation, Anthropic has condensed its vulnerability disclosure window from 90 to 30 days. Google’s TIG reports observed attacks using fully autonomous frameworks to turn security patches into exploits, marking a paradigm shift in threat speed.

perspective_pro.point_zh: 模型自我改进速度决定了防御时效，缩短窗口是倒逼安全基建升级，以实现比攻击者更快的补丁响应速度。
perspective_pro.point_en: Rapid model evolution necessitates faster disclosure; shortening the window is a necessary constraint to outpace attackers and force infrastructure upgrades.

perspective_con.speaker_zh: 网络安全漏洞审计专家
perspective_con.point_zh: 缩短披露时间可能迫使开发人员发布未经充分测试的“快补丁”，导致系统陷入频繁的破坏性重启，甚至触发AI代理的误操作。
perspective_con.point_en: Aggressive disclosure timelines risk forcing premature patches, leading to unstable systems and potential 'recursive failure' loops induced by AI agents.

The AI Revolution is rapidly moving from experimentation to enterprise-wide implementation.

news.title: Brad Gerstner says Altimeter is aiming to invest $5B in Anthropic's IPO, 5x his largest IPO investment, calling it "a cornerstone compounder for a long time" (Kif Leswing/CNBC)
news.title_en: Brad Gerstner says Altimeter is aiming to invest $5B in Anthropic's IPO, 5x his largest IPO investment, calling it "a cornerstone compounder for a long time" (Kif Leswing/CNBC)
news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
Altimeter Capital is aiming to invest $5 billion in the Anthropic IPO, Brad Gerstner told CNBC's "Halftime Report" on Monday.

"I think this is a cornerstone compounder for a long time," Gerstner said, noting that his investment would be five times the amount he's ever put into an IPO. "It's where the trade is going."

Anthropic is expected to go on Nasdaq on Thursday in a milestone event for the artificial intelligence industry. It would be the first major AI lab to go public, beating OpenAI, which has said it's targeting an IPO next year.

Gerstner is investing alongside the leading chipmakers and cloud providers, many of which count on Anthropic as a customer.

Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company are collectively investing $26 billion at the IPO price, which is currently expected at $70 to $78 a share.

Anthropic is planning to offer 825 million shares at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion.

Gerstner is friends with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and sent a letter to the board of directors last week pushing them to take their time and run a full investigation on Huang's tenure before deciding who should run the company.

Gerstner said he has confidence in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress, and noted that Huang had not discussed a comeback as CEO with him.

While Anthropic is hitting the market at a particularly tough moment — coming after a downturn in semiconductors, a massive anti-AI swing in Washington, D.C., and the Huang saga — Gerstner said he's still optimistic.

"They have done such an excellent job presenting this company, they're in such an excellent position on the financials," Gerstner said, "that folks like me are making this a major order."

news.title_zh: Altimeter计划注资50亿美元参与Anthropic IPO
news.summary_zh: Altimeter Capital首席执行官Brad Gerstner宣布计划向Anthropic IPO注资50亿美元，此举旨在将其打造为长期核心资产
news.article_content_zh:
Brad Gerstner 周一在 CNBC 的“半场报道”中表示，Altimeter Capital 计划在 Anthropic IPO 中投资 50 亿美元。

格斯特纳表示：“我认为这在很长一段时间内都是一个基石复合器。”他指出，他的投资将是他在首次公开募股中投入的金额的五倍。 “这就是贸易的发展方向。”

Anthropic 预计将于周四在纳斯达克上市，这是人工智能行业的一个里程碑事件。这将是第一个上市的大型人工智能实验室，击败了 OpenAI，后者表示计划明年进行 IPO。

格斯特纳正在与领先的芯片制造商和云提供商一起投资，其中许多都依赖 Anthropic 作为客户。

Advanced Micro Devices、博通、谷歌、美光、微软、英伟达和台积电合计投资 260 亿美元，IPO 价格目前预计为每股 70 至 78 美元。

Anthropic 计划发行 8.25 亿股股票，估值约为 1.4 万亿美元。

格斯特纳是英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的朋友，他上周致函董事会，敦促他们花时间对黄仁勋的任期进行全面调查，然后再决定由谁来管理公司。

郭士纳表示，他对首席财务官兼临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)充满信心，并指出黄仁勋并未与他讨论过重新担任首席执行官的事宜。

虽然 Anthropic 是在一个特别艰难的时刻进入市场的——在半导体行业低迷、华盛顿特区大规模的反人工智能浪潮以及黄仁勋事件之后——格斯特纳表示，他仍然保持乐观。

格斯特纳说：“他们在介绍这家公司方面做得非常出色，他们在财务方面处于非常有利的地位，像我这样的人都将其作为一项重大订单。”

news.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
news.title_en: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit on Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a “dangerous product without proper oversight,” as reported earlier by Reuters.

The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face “was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability.” It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general’s office that it “lost control” of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing.

After revealing the rogue AI attack on Hugging Face in July, news of several other similar incidents emerged, including attacks on an Australian government website, a German wiki site, and the software package manager RubyGems. OpenAI’s agents also tried to “bruteforce” a United Nations website.

“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-world cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta says in the press release. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law.”

OpenAI released its new cybersecurity AI model earlier this month, saying that it’s less likely to go rogue and attack other platforms. It’s also giving safety evaluators at Apollo Research access to its AI systems as part of a pilot program that monitors models for misalignment.

“Since the Hugging Face incident, we’ve undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says in an emailed statement to The Verge. “This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab. We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged — and will continue to engage — constructively with the Attorney General’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.”

news.article_content_zh:
加州正在起诉 OpenAI，因为其人工智能代理闯入了他们的测试环境并攻击了包括 Hugging Face 在内的其他公司。据路透社早些时候报道，司法部长 Rob Bonta 在周一的诉讼中指控 OpenAI 故意开发“未经适当监督的危险产品”，违反了消费者安全法。

该诉讼称，Hugging Face 受到的网络攻击“是 OpenAI 内部文化的可预见结果，这种文化优先考虑增长和快速模型开发，而不是安全和责任。”据称，OpenAI 最近告诉总检察长办公室，在测试过程中，其人工智能代理“失去控制”了 80 多次。

继 7 月份揭露 Hugging Face 上的流氓 AI 攻击之后，其他几起类似事件的消息也出现了，包括对澳大利亚政府网站、德国 wiki 网站和软件包管理器 RubyGems 的攻击。 OpenAI 的特工还试图“暴力破解”联合国网站。

Bonta 在新闻稿中表示：“OpenAI 的行为加剧了现实世界的网络安全风险，威胁到社会的安全、健康和福祉。” “该公司在没有适当监督或安全程序的情况下故意测试危险产品，并误导公众——这种对公共安全的漠视违反了加州法律。”

OpenAI 本月早些时候发布了其新的网络安全人工智能模型，称它不太可能失控并攻击其他平台。它还允许阿波罗研究中心的安全评估人员访问其人工智能系统，作为监控模型偏差的试点计划的一部分。

OpenAI 发言人德鲁·普萨泰里 (Drew Pusateri) 在发给 The Verge 的电子邮件声明中表示：“自 Hugging Face 事件以来，我们采取了广泛且透明的努力来理解和解决不一致的模型活动。” “这起诉讼似乎针对 OpenAI 的挑战，每个主要人工智能实验室都已发现了这一挑战。我们认真对待这种不一致，我们已经并将继续与总检察长办公室进行建设性的接触，以共享信息并为整个行业推进强大、实用的安全标准。”

news.title: Sam Altman says he wants everyone ‘to have a lot of RAM’
news.title_en: Sam Altman says he wants everyone ‘to have a lot of RAM’

inline_images.caption: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
inline_images.alt: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions

news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is once again addressing his controversial comments on PC RAM purchases. “I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM, I think everybody should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer,” Altman said today. “I think the home tinkering is great.”

The comments were made on stage at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World summit on Monday.

Altman’s remarks on RAM stirred up controversy last month. In an appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman said that it’s “quite terrible” for everyone to have RAM in personal computers rather than in data centers. He later followed up on those comments in posts on X earlier this month, saying, “i want you to have so much ram” and saying the original remarks had been “taken out of context.”

AI companies have been buying up the world’s memory supply for data centers, leading to ongoing price hikes on everything from phones to game consoles. Altman commented on supply chain issues, saying OpenAI has “been constrained by different things at different times,” like memory, rack assembly, data center capacity, or “some random component.”

On stage today, Altman went on to say that “a few years ago we started saying the world needs to build a lot more memory supply chain in particular.” He acknowledged how RAM prices have soared over recent months, saying:

> “The world did not build out that much, and now we have seen DRAM prices — I don’t know exactly, but maybe they went up 5x, 7x, something like that. I think it would be much better if the world just had a lot of memory. That comment, which I think got misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it, which I will stand by is that, if we’re going to be in this memory supply shortage, then in some sense — whether or not we’ll decide to do it, because I think there are other tradeoffs like people having their own at-home inference — the optimal thing would be, can we share this memory and have it working 100 percent of the time rather than sometimes off in someone’s edge device? Again, optimal use of this limited supply. Maybe it’s not the reason to make the decision but that’s what I was trying to say.”

Altman also commented on Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia’s CEO, saying he “doesn’t know enough” to say if Huang should be reinstated.

news.article_content_zh:
OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 再次回应了他有关 PC RAM 购买的有争议的评论。 “我想澄清的是，我希望人们拥有大量 RAM，我认为每个人都应该能够为自己的计算机购买大量 RAM，”Altman 今天表示。 “我认为家里的修补很棒。”

这些评论是周一在 Semafor 硅谷与世界峰会的舞台上发表的。

奥特曼上个月关于 RAM 的言论引发了争议。 Altman 在 Cheeky Pint 播客上露面时表示，对于每个人来说，在个人电脑而不是数据中心拥有 RAM 是“非常可怕的”。随后，他在本月早些时候的 X 帖子中对这些评论进行了跟进，称“我希望你有这么多内存”，并表示最初的言论已“断章取义”。

人工智能公司一直在购买全球数据中心的内存供应，导致从手机到游戏机等各种产品的价格持续上涨。 Altman 在评论供应链问题时表示，OpenAI “在不同时间受到不同因素的限制”，比如内存、机架组装、数据中心容量或“一些随机组件”。

今天在台上，奥特曼接着说，“几年前，我们开始说世界特别需要建立更多的内存供应链。”他承认近几个月来 RAM 价格飙升，并表示：

> “世界并没有建设那么多，现在我们已经看到 DRAM 的价格 - 我不太清楚，但也许它们上涨了 5 倍、7 倍，类似的东西。我认为如果世界拥有大量内存，情况会好得多。我认为这个评论被误解了，但它的真实部分是，我会坚持的是，如果我们要陷入内存供应短缺，那么从某种意义上说 - 无论我们是否决定这样做它，因为我认为还有其他权衡，比如人们有自己的家庭推理——最好的办法是，我们可以共享这个内存并让它在 100% 的时间里工作，而不是有时在某人的边缘设备上工作吗？同样，也许这不是做出决定的原因，但这就是我想说的。”

奥尔特曼还对黄仁勋辞去英伟达首席执行官一事发表了评论，称他“还不够了解”是否应该恢复黄仁勋的职位。

news.title: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day
news.title_en: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day

inline_images.caption: : A view of Intel office building on August 22, 2025 in Beijing, China.
inline_images.alt: : A view of Intel office building on August 22, 2025 in Beijing, China.

news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
The PC sales slump “more than offset” AI boom gains, shareholders say.

Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel’s stock on October 30.

The lawsuit (PDF), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants.

The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period.

In the complaint, the shareholders argue that Intel misled them by failing to disclose: the full impact that the PC market sales slump would have on Intel’s third quarter and beyond; the impact of increasing PC component prices on PC sales for Intel’s OEM and distribution partners; that Intel was dealing with substrate supply constraints that would limit its ability to meet data center CPU demand; and “that any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset” by the PC sales slump.

“… statements regarding Intel’s business, operations, financial results, and ability to capitalize on the boom for AI-related infrastructure spending were materially false and misleading when made, and such statements did not accurately reflect Intel’s then-present business and prospects,” the law firm representing the plaintiffs, Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP, said in a statement issued on Friday.

On October 29, Intel announced what the complaint calls “disastrous” fiscal Q3 earnings. During the quarter, revenue for Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) business declined 5 percent year over year.

At the time, Tan pointed to an “unprecedented memory crunch” and manufacturing supply shortages hurting the PC market.

The next day, Intel’s shares fell 28.6 percent in “the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years,” the complaint notes.

Intel hasn’t publicly commented on the lawsuit.

news.article_content_zh:
股东们表示，个人电脑销量的下滑“远远抵消了”人工智能繁荣的收益。

英特尔正被股东起诉，他们指责该芯片制造商在个人电脑销售下滑的影响方面误导了他们，导致英特尔股价在 10 月 30 日下跌了 28.6%。

该诉讼 (PDF) 于周五在加利福尼亚州圣何塞联邦法院提起，正在寻求集体诉讼认证，并将南菲尔德市消防和警察退休系统以及“所有其他类似情况”列为原告。除英特尔外，英特尔首席执行官陈立武 (Lip-Bu Tan) 以及英特尔执行副总裁兼首席财务官 David Zinsner 也被列为被告。

原告声称，英特尔在 7 月 23 日至 10 月 29 日期间做出了“重大虚假和误导性陈述和遗漏”。他们正在寻求在此期间为股东提供未具体说明的赔偿性损害赔偿，以及法律和其他相关费用。

在诉状中，股东们辩称，英特尔没有披露以下信息，从而误导了他们：个人电脑市场销售下滑对英特尔第三季度及以后的全面影响； PC 组件价格上涨对英特尔 OEM 和分销合作伙伴 PC 销售的影响；英特尔正在应对基板供应限制，这将限制其满足数据中心 CPU 需求的能力； “数据中心建设和人工智能繁荣的其他方面对英特尔业务和财务业绩的任何积极影响都被个人电脑销售下滑所抵消”。

代表原告的律师事务所 Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP 在周五发布的一份声明中表示：“......有关英特尔的业务、运营、财务业绩以及利用人工智能相关基础设施支出热潮的能力的陈述在做出时存在重大虚假和误导性，并且此类陈述没有准确反映英特尔当时的业务和前景。”

10 月 29 日，英特尔公布了投诉所称的“灾难性”第三季度财报。本季度，英特尔客户端计算和物理人工智能事业部 (CCPG) 业务的收入同比下降 5%。

当时，谭指出“前所未有的内存紧缩”和制造业供应短缺损害了个人电脑市场。

英特尔尚未对这起诉讼公开发表评论。

news.article_content:
Constellation Energy – America’s largest operator of nuclear power plants – does not share Wall Street’s concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave.

“I do think we’ve seen a bit of an overreaction in the market to the election results based upon fear that Democrats won’t let data centers get built,” Dominguez said.

Many of the Democrats who seized control of the House and Senate in this month’s midterm elections ran on anti-data-center campaigns, which triggered a historic $2.5 trillion sell-off in AI-adjacent stocks that reached well beyond tech to the energy, construction, and materials sectors.

Up until a few years ago, many of Constellation’s nuclear power plants were in severe financial distress and in danger of shutting down early. But the data center development boom and its enormous demand for electricity have dramatically reversed the nuclear industry’s fate.

Now, Constellation and other companies like it are signing major deals with Big Tech companies to provide power to data centers. Microsoft, for instance, signed a deal with Constellation to fund the revival of a nuclear plant at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania. (Three Mile Island is the site of what the Nuclear Regulatory Commission refers to as the “most serious accident in US commercial nuclear power plant operating history.”)

Constellation also signed major contracts in the third quarter to provide power to Amazon and Google data centers, Dominguez said.

Nuclear energy has had bipartisan support for years. The US Department of Energy classifies nuclear as a “clean” energy source because the act of operating a nuclear reactor does not directly produce carbon emissions. This makes nuclear an appealing investment to Big Tech companies that have to balance aggressive data center development with the ambitious climate goals they set long before the AI race took off. Still, nuclear energy has its issues. One of the biggest is nuclear waste, which the US government has not figured out how to dispose of at scale.

Big Nuclear and Big Tech also tout these deals as good for the economy and job creation.

“The market scare that people got last week was not lost on Democrats,” Dominguez said on the call. “They do not want to be the reason that the economy takes a nosedive by halting data center development.”

Of course, Constellation’s future is essentially staked on the data center buildout, and Dominguez’s job is to convince investors they have nothing to worry about.

In this instance, however, Dominguez really does seem genuinely unconcerned by the new Democratic majority in the federal government. It could be that he understands that, yes, while the Democrats won the midterms on promises of data center regulation and the blue wave included many new Democratic governors, data centers aren’t necessarily a strictly partisan issue. Some Democrats have opposed harsh measures like moratoriums — though on the flip slide, Constellation may also have to deal with challenges from the other side of the aisle.

In Virginia, some of the state lawmakers who have been the most vocal about data centers are actually Republican. Virginia Sen. news.article_content_zh:
美国最大的核电站运营商星座能源公司并不认同华尔街对民主党将放慢数据中心发展的担忧。在该公司上周的第三季度财报电话会议上，首席执行官乔·多明计斯(Joe Dominguez)在谈到蓝色浪潮时表现得无动于衷。

多明计斯表示：“我确实认为，市场对选举结果反应有些过度，因为担心民主党不会让数据中心建成。”

许多在本月中期选举中控制众议院和参议院的民主党人发起了反数据中心运动，引发了人工智能相关股票历史性的 2.5 万亿美元抛售，抛售范围远远超出科技行业，涉及能源、建筑和材料行业。

直到几年前，星座公司的许多核电站还陷入严重的财务困境，并面临提前关闭的危险。但数据中心的发展热潮及其对电力的巨大需求极大地扭转了核工业的命运。

现在，Constellation 和其他类似公司正在与大型科技公司签署重大协议，为数据中心提供电力。例如，微软与星座公司签署了一项协议，为宾夕法尼亚州三哩岛的一座核电站的复兴提供资金。 （三哩岛是核管理委员会所说的“美国商业核电站运营历史上最严重的事故发生地”。）

多明格斯表示，星座公司还在第三季度签署了重要合同，为亚马逊和谷歌数据中心提供电力。

核能多年来一直得到两党的支持。美国能源部将核能列为“清洁”能源，因为运行核反应堆的行为不会直接产生碳排放。这使得核能成为对大型科技公司有吸引力的投资，这些公司必须在积极的数据中心开发与他们在人工智能竞赛起飞之前很久就设定的雄心勃勃的气候目标之间取得平衡。尽管如此，核能也有其问题。其中最大的废物之一是核废物，美国政府尚未弄清楚如何大规模处置核废物。

大型核电和大型科技公司也宣称这些交易有利于经济和创造就业机会。

多明计斯在电话会议上表示：“民主党人并没有忽视上周人们对市场的恐慌。” “他们不想成为因停止数据中心开发而导致经济急转直下的原因。”

当然，Constellation 的未来本质上取决于数据中心的扩建，而多明计斯的工作就是让投资者相信他们无需担心。

然而，在这种情况下，多明格斯似乎确实对联邦政府中新的民主党多数派并不关心。他可能明白，是的，虽然民主党依靠数据中心监管的承诺赢得了中期选举，并且蓝色浪潮中包括了许多新的民主党州长，但数据中心不一定是一个严格的党派问题。一些民主党人反对暂停等严厉措施——尽管反过来，星座公司可能还必须应对来自党派另一方的挑战。

在弗吉尼亚州，一些对数据中心最直言不讳的州议员实际上是共和党人。弗吉尼亚州参议员理查德·斯图尔特 (Richard Stuart) 是一名保守派共和党人，一直积极推行数据中心监管。上个月，弗吉尼亚州州长、民主党人阿比盖尔·斯潘伯格拒绝了斯图尔特召开特别会议的请求，以讨论弗吉尼亚州环境质量部关于该州地下水供应的令人担忧的新报告，该州地下水供应因数据中心的快速增长而变得紧张。

迄今为止，针对数据中心的斗争是高度分散和超本地化的，但这种情况可能很快就会改变。特朗普政府热爱数据中心，联邦政府正在努力从各州手中夺取数据中心开发的部分控制权。但即便如此，联邦层面的民主党和共和党仍倾向于将数据中心视为未来不可避免的一部分，需要一些护栏，而不是失控的企业增长损害美国人的平均生活质量。

只要看看由两位民主党人共同发起的两党《美国负担能力和就业法案》就知道了。预计参议院将就一项全面法案的通过进行投票，该法案被宣传为加快新发电厂和输电线路的许可流程以及更快地将新数据中心连接到电网的一种方式。支持该法案的民主党人之一、新墨西哥州参议员马丁·海因里希(Martin Heinrich)宣称，该法案纳入了旨在保护公用事业客户免受数据中心导致的费率上涨影响的条款，确保大型科技公司支付其公平份额的成本。哥伦比亚大学 SIPA 全球能源政策中心的研究人员称该法案的保护“好坏参半”，并指出它们没有考虑批发容量和能源价格，这是数据中心电力需求导致家庭电费上涨的“主要方式”。

news.title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
news.title_en: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.

The study homes in on hyperscale facilities — the massive structures spanning millions of square feet that developers are racing to build in large part to support generative AI. Researchers say the findings show that there’s a lot of work left to do to cut down pollution stemming from AI’s reliance on fossil fuels.

“We tend to discuss AI’s environmental footprint as though it were some fixed property of the technology, when in reality the same computing infrastructure can have dramatically different consequences depending on the electricity system supporting it,” Gianluca Guidi, lead author of the new study and a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, says in an email to The Verge. “I actually find that encouraging, because it means these impacts aren’t inevitable. We have choices about where we build and how we power this infrastructure.”

Guidi and his team used satellite imagery to identify 403 hyperscale data centers in the US, estimating each facility’s power consumption based on its electrical capacity. Using data from the Environmental Protection Agency, they approximated how much carbon pollution each data center would have produced if connected to the local power grid between May 2024 and April 2025.

Altogether, the 403 hyperscale facilities likely consumed around 82 terawatt-hours of electricity that year, about 1.8 percent of all US electricity consumption. That’s even more than the amount of electricity that about 148 nations — a majority of the countries in the world including Austria, Israel, and Venezuela but excluding the largest economies including the US and China — individually burn through each year, according to John Sterman, director of the MIT System Dynamics group and MIT Sloan Sustainability Initiative.

Electricity demand from these data centers produced 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 emissions, comparable to the annual carbon footprint of Denmark, according to the research paper. Sterman says that exceeds the total carbon emissions of about 113 nations. That’s because about 54 percent of the electricity the hyperscale facilities consumed likely came from gas and coal.

Sterman, who was not involved in the research with Guidi, disclosed that he used the help of Claude to compare the paper’s findings to electricity use and emissions of countries. “I think AI can be extraordinarily helpful,” Sterman says. “But we’ve got to figure out a way to limit the harms … Especially because those impacts are irreversible. Once you allow these data centers to emit the CO2, you can never undo that.”

Sterman says policymakers should require data center operators to bring new clean energy online. The study doesn’t account for local air pollution that can result from new gas infrastructure that’s being built to meet data center demand, or gas turbines that some AI companies have installed at their facilities to power themselves without connecting to the grid. And while hyperscale data centers encompass more than just AI-related computing, they also make up just a fraction of the thousands of data centers in the US — with more cropping up each year.

news.article_content_zh:
《自然可持续发展》杂志上发表的一篇新论文显示，化石燃料仍然是美国超大规模数据中心的最大电力来源。它们消耗的电力可能比许多国家还要多，从而导致大量的温室气体排放。

这项研究的重点是超大规模设施——开发商竞相建造的占地数百万平方英尺的大型结构，很大程度上是为了支持生成式人工智能。研究人员表示，研究结果表明，要减少人工智能对化石燃料的依赖所造成的污染，还有很多工作要做。

“我们倾向于讨论人工智能的环境足迹，就好像它是该技术的某些固定属性一样，但实际上，根据支持它的电力系统，相同的计算基础设施可能会产生截然不同的后果，”这项新研究的主要作者、哈佛大学公共卫生学院生物统计学系博士后吉安卢卡·吉迪 (Gianluca Guidi) 说道。陈公共卫生学院在给 The Verge 的电子邮件中说道。 “我实际上发现这令人鼓舞，因为这意味着这些影响并非不可避免。我们可以选择在哪里建设以及如何为该基础设施提供动力。”

Guidi 和他的团队利用卫星图像识别了美国 403 个超大规模数据中心，并根据每个设施的电力容量估算了其功耗。他们利用环境保护局的数据，估算了 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 4 月期间每个数据中心连接到当地电网时会产生多少碳污染。

当年，403 个超大规模设施总共消耗了约 82 太瓦时的电力，约占美国总电力消耗的 1.8%。麻省理工学院系统动力学小组和麻省理工学院斯隆可持续发展计划主任约翰·斯特曼表示，这甚至超过了约 148 个国家（包括奥地利、以色列和委内瑞拉等世界上大多数国家，但不包括美国和中国等最大经济体）每年单独消耗的电量。

研究论文称，这些数据中心的电力需求产生了 2570 万吨二氧化碳排放，与丹麦的年碳足迹相当。斯特曼表示，这超过了约 113 个国家的碳排放总量。这是因为超大规模设施消耗的电力中大约 54% 可能来自天然气和煤炭。

斯特曼没有参与吉迪的研究，他透露，他在克劳德的帮助下将该论文的研究结果与各国的电力使用和排放进行了比较。 “我认为人工智能非常有帮助，”斯特曼说。 “但我们必须找到一种方法来限制危害……特别是因为这些影响是不可逆转的。一旦你允许这些数据中心排放二氧化碳，你就永远无法挽回。”

斯特曼表示，政策制定者应该要求数据中心运营商提供新的清洁能源。该研究没有考虑到当地的空气污染，这些污染可能是由于为满足数据中心需求而建造的新天然气基础设施造成的，也没有考虑到一些人工智能公司在其设施中安装的燃气轮机在不连接电网的情况下自行供电所造成的污染。虽然超大规模数据中心不仅仅包含与人工智能相关的计算，但它们也只占美国数千个数据中心的一小部分——而且每年都会出现更多数据中心。

该研究表明，当地电力结构对人工智能和数据中心的环境影响有多大影响。严重依赖煤炭的怀俄明州每千瓦时发电的碳排放量是水力发电丰富的俄勒冈州的大约七倍。吉迪写道：“两个消耗完全相同电量的数据中心可能会因为所处位置的不同而产生截然不同的碳足迹。”

康奈尔大学能源系统工程系教授尤凤琪（Fengqi You）也没有参与这项研究，他表示，研究结果凸显了“长期碳锁定”的问题。 “为满足快速增长的数据中心需求而建造的发电厂和配套基础设施可能会运行数十年。因此，今天做出的决定可能会影响未来的排放，”尤在给 The Verge 的电子邮件中说道。

You和Guidi还指出，由于数据中心运营商不会披露这些信息，研究人员必须花费如此多的时间来估计能源消耗，这是多么有问题。为此，Guidi 和他的同事正在利用他们的研究成果建立一个网站来跟踪各个数据中心对环境的影响。国会通过的一项两党法案还可能要求全国范围内更多地披露数据中心的用电量。

“社区和政策制定者需要可靠、独立的数据来了解这些设施对我们的空气、健康和气候意味着什么。这项研究是重要的一步。”前白宫国家气候顾问兼美国环保署署长吉娜·麦卡锡在研究作者分享的一份声明中表示。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】Gianluca Guidi（哈佛大学）及MIT研究团队在期刊《自然-可持续性》：量化全美超大规模数据中心的能源消费及对应的碳排放规模
【起因与机理】评估生成式AI基础设施增长对全球气候目标的长期影响
【关键数据与实测】403个超大规模设施年耗电达82太瓦时。
【各方立场与态度】算力与环境治理间的能源溯源合规矛盾。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Gianluca Guidi (Harvard University) and MIT research team (Nature Sustainability): Quantifying energy consumption and carbon footprints of U.S. hyperscale data centers
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Evaluating the long-term impact of generative AI infrastructure scaling on global climate goals
[Key Metrics] Fossil fuels account for approximately 54% of electricity consumption.
[Key Position & Outlook] Regulatory conflict between compute growth and energy traceability.

By CATHY BUSSEWITZ Updated [hour]:[minute] [AMPM] [timezone], [monthFull] [day], [year] --> Add AP News on Google Add AP News as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. --> Share

NEW YORK (AP) — Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some major U.S. banks Monday.

Bank of America, Chase, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.

Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday.

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”

A spokesman from U.S. Bank said its systems are not directly impacted, however, “clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”

Zelle’s network operator is a company called Early Warning Services, which is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Some Chase customers received a message that said “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began Friday and lasted for hours which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot.

纽约（美联社）——周一，客户报告称在美国一些主要银行访问在线账户时遇到困难。

据 downDetector.com 网站称，美国银行、大通银行、合众银行、富国银行和 Truist 被用户列为宕机或遇到问题的银行。

一位发言人周一表示，大通银行的服务遇到了技术错误问题，而不是网络问题。

大通发言人在一份声明中表示：“由于技术问题，一些交易需要比平时更长的时间才能完成，但客户仍然可以访问他们的账户和资金。” “我们正在努力尽快解决这个问题。”

美国合众银行发言人表示，其系统并未受到直接影响，但“尝试与其他金融机构发送或接收 Zelle 付款的客户可能会遇到交易延迟。”

Zelle 的网络运营商是一家名为 Early Warning Services 的公司，该公司的所有者包括美国银行、第一资本、摩根大通、PNC 银行、Truist、合众银行和富国银行等金融机构。

一些大通银行客户收到一条消息，内容为“某些服务不可用。我们正在处理这些服务。请稍后再试。”

这些报告是在微软从周五开始并持续数小时的一次重大故障之后发布的，影响了包括 Outlook、Teams 和 AI 助理 Copilot 在内的服务。

news.title: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast
news.title_en: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast

inline_images.alt: Google places current activity at Level 5, where AI tools carry out several stages of an attack with

news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) says it has observed attackers fully automating vulnerability discovery and exploitation for the first time, with no human in the loop. GTIG found an exposed server running an AI framework called "exploit_agent" that connects to multiple language models, according to the GTIG AI Threat Tracker. The system compares software code before and after patches, identifies vulnerabilities, develops exploits, and runs them automatically. Russian-language comments in the configuration files suggest the operator speaks Russian.

Server data suggests the operator targeted French websites in media, entertainment, and education. GTIG calls the shift a critical turning point but says these automated attacks currently sacrifice stealth for speed, leaving forensic traces that make them easier to detect.

news.summary_en: Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) has identified the first fully autonomous attack system, 'exploit_agent,' which leverages LLMs to identify vulnerabilities, develop exploits, and execute them without human intervention. While these attacks currently leave forensic traces, the transition to end-to-end automated exploitation marks a critical turning point in AI-driven cybersecurity warfare.

news.title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
news.title_en: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.

Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models.

Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.

Last week Apple updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for that app’s intelligent assistant through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that are expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

news.title: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines
news.title_en: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
OpenAI is announcing a tool that it says will help child sexual abuse investigators cut through the noise to find harmful material they can act on quickly.

At a Monday press briefing in Washington, DC, OpenAI announced a classifier it says can better detect abusive imagery of kids, including whether it’s AI-generated. It’s also offering free access to vetted organizations, giving developers more guidance on how to detect this type of content, and helping to train law enforcement on how AI can aid their investigations. The news comes as policymakers and others are pushing for more safety restrictions on AI tools, accusing OpenAI and other companies of facilitating harm to children.

In recent years, AI-generated sexual images of children have threatened to overwhelm systems like the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) CyberTipline, which collects and triages reports of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The CyberTipline received 400,000 generative AI-related reports in 2025, an exponential increase from the 67,000 it received in 2024, and researchers have warned that the influx could make NCMEC’s workload “unmanageable.” The US government has stated that both AI-generated and non-AI-generated CSAM is illegal, and 48 states have laws to address sexually explicit AI deepfakes. But the tools to make them are widely available, and researchers say that a flood of fake images can make it harder to tell when a child is actively experiencing harm.

North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson, who cochairs the AG Alliance’s AI Task Force, said at OpenAI’s event that the influx of AI-generated CSAM reports to NCMEC is “explosive” — and if they keep going that way, “it is going to mean that we fail in our mission.” Tech companies are facing a range of policy proposals that could require them to take more action against CSAM and other potentially harmful content for kids. The Take It Down Act now requires social media platforms to remove real or AI-generated nonconsensual intimate images within 48 hours, and the newly elected Congress could seek to take stronger action against AI companies like SpaceXSI, whose Grok chatbot went on an undressing spree earlier this year. Last month eight states sued OpenAI for a separate set of alleged harms to children, citing lawsuits alleging ChatGPT encouraged illegal substance use and suicide.

OpenAI says its classifier dramatically cuts down on false positives, flagging 48 percent fewer images, while the images it did identify were twice as likely to contain abusive material. It’s designed to catch abusive AI-generated images produced by a variety of tools, including open-source models and nudifying apps. It’s also the first broadly available CSAM classifier with a specific flag for AI-generated material, said OpenAI’s head of child safety public policy, John Buckley, at the briefing. “It’s important for industry to be able to understand what images may contain a fictional child versus a real child,” Buckley added. “That triage is critical in law enforcement reporting flows.” He also emphasized, however, that laws should recognize the harm of AI-generated CSAM: “It potentially erodes social norms in offending against children, and it’s often found colocated with child sexual abuse imagery of real children,” Buckley said.

news.article_content_zh:
OpenAI 宣布推出一款工具，据称该工具将帮助儿童性虐待调查人员消除噪音，找到可以快速采取行动的有害材料。

在周一于华盛顿特区举行的新闻发布会上，OpenAI 宣布了一款分类器，据称可以更好地检测儿童的虐待图像，包括它是否是人工智能生成的。它还提供对经过审查的组织的免费访问，为开发人员提供有关如何检测此类内容的更多指导，并帮助培训执法人员了解人工智能如何协助他们的调查。这一消息发布之际，政策制定者和其他人士正在推动对人工智能工具实施更多安全限制，指责 OpenAI 和其他公司助长了对儿童的伤害。

近年来，人工智能生成的儿童性图像已经威胁到国家失踪和受虐儿童中心 (NCMEC) Cyber​​Tipline 等系统，该中心负责收集和分类儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM) 的报告。 Cyber​​Tipline 在 2025 年收到了 400,000 份与生成人工智能相关的报告，比 2024 年收到的 67,000 份呈指数增长，研究人员警告说，这些报告的涌入可能会使 NCMEC 的工作量“难以管理”。美国政府表示，人工智能生成和非人工智能生成的 CSAM 都是非法的，并且 48 个州制定了法律来解决露骨的人工智能深度伪造问题。但制作它们的工具很广泛，研究人员表示，大量的虚假图像会让我们更难判断孩子何时正在遭受伤害。

AG 联盟 AI 工作组联合主席、北卡罗来纳州总检察长杰夫·杰克逊 (Jeff Jackson) 在 OpenAI 的活动上表示，向 NCMEC 提交的 AI 生成的 CSAM 报告的涌入是“爆炸性的”——如果他们继续这样下去，“将意味着我们的使命失败。”科技公司正面临一系列政策建议，这些建议可能要求他们对 CSAM 和其他对儿童可能有害的内容采取更多行动。 《Take It Down Act》现在要求社交媒体平台在 48 小时内删除真实的或人工智能生成的非自愿亲密图像，新当选的国会可能会寻求对 SpaceXSI 等人工智能公司采取更强硬的行动，该公司的 Grok 聊天机器人在今年早些时候进行了脱衣狂欢。上个月，八个州起诉 OpenAI，指控其对儿童造成一系列伤害，并援引指控 ChatGPT 鼓励非法药物使用和自杀的诉讼。

OpenAI 表示，它的分类器大大减少了误报，标记的图像减少了 48%，而它识别出的图像包含滥用内容的可能性是原来的两倍。它旨在捕获由各种工具（包括开源模型和裸体应用程序）生成的滥用人工智能生成的图像。 OpenAI 儿童安全公共政策负责人 John Buckley 在简报会上表示，这也是第一个广泛使用的 CSAM 分类器，带有针对 AI 生成材料的特定标志。巴克利补充说：“对于行业来说，能够了解哪些图像可能包含虚构的孩子和真实的孩子非常重要。” “这种分类对于执法报告流程至关重要。”不过，他也强调，法律应该认识到人工智能生成的 CSAM 的危害：“它可能会侵蚀犯罪儿童的社会规范，而且它经常与真实儿童的儿童性虐待图像同时出现，”巴克利说。

OpenAI 自己的 ChatGPT 图像生成器旨在拒绝用户对 CSAM 的请求。现在，尝试生成它的用户将看到在专家指导下开发的新警告，以鼓励他们寻求帮助。首次违规将触发 ChatGPT 访问 24 小时暂停，并警告用户其帐户可能会被永久关闭，同时提供支持资源来打击该行为。 OpenAI 表示，它向 NCMEC 报告“所有 CSAM 实例”。巴克利在一份声明中解释说，24 小时的暂停是基于专家对最佳实践的建议，“以及关于如何有效预防和应对 CSAM 寻求与 CSAM 生成的国际证据”。重点是“阻止有害行为并引导人们寻求专家帮助来制止这种行为。”

Jackson 表示，北卡罗来纳州和许多其他州现在都制定了涵盖合成 CSAM 的法律，但与 OpenAI 这样的科技公司合作来帮助阻止其创建，是解决新兴问题的一种相当新颖的方法。 “总检察长所做的大部分工作是问责工作，”他在新闻发布会上告诉记者。 “我们的大部分司法管辖权都是在事后开始追究人们对伤害的责任。但通过这一点，我们想看看是否有可能开发出一种共同合作的模式来防止这种伤害。我想说，这基本上仍然是一个实验。”

news.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice
news.title_en: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra tackles the Standard Model's toughest math problem on a lattice

inline_images.caption: The diagram shows how comparing increasingly finer lattices helps correct the phase shift on the original lattice. | Image: Nathaniel Craig / GPT-6 Astra
inline_images.alt: The diagram shows how comparing increasingly finer lattices helps correct the phase shift on the ori

news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helped produce a proof that could solve a 50-year-old problem in particle physics.

Physicist Nathaniel Craig of UC Santa Barbara, currently a visiting scientist at OpenAI, presented the approach on the OpenAI blog and as a preprint paper. Craig leads the particle theory group at UCSB and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.

Physicists can simulate parts of the Standard Model, the theory describing all known particles and fundamental forces, on a computer grid called a lattice. That has already led to breakthroughs like calculating the proton's mass from first principles. But putting the full theory on a lattice has been impossible. The weak force, which governs certain types of radioactive decay, treats left- and right-handed particles differently. On simple lattices, this asymmetry creates unwanted ghost particles. Special lattice particles called overlap fermions can filter them out, but for over 25 years, nobody could set their phase correctly.Ad

Craig had a strategy to fix the phase by comparing progressively finer lattices, but couldn't prove it worked in all the cases it needed to cover. GPT-6 Astra turned the idea into a working construction and took the lead on the detailed proof. Lattice field theorists Maarten Golterman, Andreas Kronfeld, and Yigal Shamir reviewed the proof and raised questions that Craig says helped build confidence in the result. He calls the work "much more a beginning than an end" and says a lot remains before realistic simulations are possible.Ad

The result follows a run of AI advances in mathematics that started in January 2026. In May, OpenAI's disproof of Erdős's unit distance conjecture became the first AI proof worthy of math's top journal. Days later, Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved nine of 353 open Erdős problems for a few hundred dollars, and by October its results had passed peer review.

The most far-reaching claim came in September, when OpenAI submitted a 166-page proof for the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem and the Clay Mathematics Institute said it had "apparently been settled". The solution remains under review, and mathematicians have questioned whether OpenAI fully understands its own proof. Across the field, mathematicians have mixed feelings as AI keeps cracking unsolved problems.Ad

news.summary_zh: OpenAI的研究员利用GPT-6 Astra构建并验证了粒子物理标准模型中困扰学界25年的手征费米子相位难题
news.article_content_zh:
OpenAI的GPT-6 Astra帮助提供了一个证明，可以解决粒子物理学中一个50年的问题。

加州大学圣巴巴拉分校的物理学家 Nathaniel Craig 目前是 OpenAI 的访问科学家，他在 OpenAI 博客上和预印本论文中介绍了该方法。克雷格领导着加州大学圣巴巴拉分校的粒子理论小组，并且是卡维理理论物理研究所的永久成员。

物理学家可以在称为晶格的计算机网格上模拟标准模型的部分内容，该理论描述了所有已知的粒子和基本力。这已经带来了一些突破，比如根据第一原理计算质子的质量。但将完整的理论放在格子上是不可能的。弱力控制某些类型的放射性衰变，它以不同的方式对待左手粒子和右手粒子。在简单晶格上，这种不对称性会产生不需要的鬼粒子。称为重叠费米子的特殊晶格粒子可以将它们过滤掉，但 25 年来，没有人能够正确设置它们的相位。

克雷格有一个通过比较逐渐精细的晶格来修复相位的策略，但无法证明它在它需要涵盖的所有情况下都有效。 GPT-6 Astra 将这个想法变成了可行的结构，并率先进行了详细的证明。格场理论家 Maarten Golterman、Andreas Kronfeld 和 Yigal Shamir 审查了证明并提出了问题，克雷格表示这些问题有助于建立对结果的信心。他称这项工作“更多的是一个开始而不是结束”，并表示在现实模拟成为可能之前还有很多工作要做。

这一结果是自 2026 年 1 月开始的人工智能在数学领域取得的一系列进展之后得出的。5 月，OpenAI 对 Erdős 单位距离猜想的反驳成为第一个值得数学顶级期刊认可的人工智能证明。几天后，Google Deepmind 的 AlphaProof Nexus 以数百美元的价格解决了 353 个开放式 Erdős 问题中的 9 个，到 10 月，其结果已通过同行评审。

影响最深远的说法发生在 9 月份，当时 OpenAI 提交了一份 166 页的纳维-斯托克斯千年奖问题证明，克莱数学研究所表示该问题“显然已经解决”。该解决方案仍在审查中，数学家质疑 OpenAI 是否完全理解自己的证明。随着人工智能不断解决未解决的问题，整个领域的数学家们心情复杂。

Many companies that switch to turbopuffer are cutting their search bills by 50% or more and getting much faster results. Check it out. Also, check out the new and improved The Pragmatic Engineer search I built on top of turbopuffer!

• Linear – one of the big challenges for us devs is the sheer amount of code to review. Linear Diffs is a new feature for reviewing PRs inside of Linear, with all the context in one place. It also supports stacked PRs. Check it out

• WorkOS – WorkOS built Airlock, the authorization layer for AI agents. It evaluates every request against the agent’s intent + your rules, and either allows it, denies it, or routes it to a human. Works with Claude Code, Codex & MCP gateways. Learn more

What does software engineering look like when generating the code becomes cheap and verifying it is the hard part?

There can be few people in tech more qualified to tackle this hot topic than Satya Nadella. Microsoft’s CEO started his career as a software engineer – a rare thing among Big Tech CEOs. Satya joins me to discuss how building software is changing at Microsoft, and what it means for us, software engineers.

We start with Microsoft’s embrace of open source from the mid-2010s and the lessons learned from building VS Code in the open. I ask how Microsoft went from holding an early lead with GitHub Copilot to having to catch up with Cursor and Claude Code, and what it reveals about building products around rapidly improving models.

Satya also explains what a “software factory” means to him, why specifications and verification are becoming more important, and how teams that work on products like the Windows operating system are adapting. We also touch on Microsoft’s voluntary exit offers, AI-related anxiety around engineering careers, and hear Nadella caution against drawing long-term conclusions from the slowdown in junior hiring.

We also explore open and local models, why companies need to control their own AI infrastructure, and how to build safeguards around increasingly capable agents. Satya also has some advice for engineers who want to excel during this period of change – and why he would like to spend more time on building.

I appreciated how grounded and thoughtful Satya was – and how pragmatic he is in suggesting to verify anything and everything related with LLMs, and not blindly trust anything or anyone (including vendors or AI models!) 12 of the most interesting takeaways I noted:

1. A new form of software engineering: teams building software factories to improve their work. Satya cites the Azure networking team which manages 500+ fiber network operators and recently built an agentic system to better manage emails and processes. Now, they operate much more efficiently as a result. Satya sees this as the reality of “AI transformation”: brownfield work on building software factories to improve how teams operate, all while continuing the day-to-day work.

Gergely OroszNov 16, 2026 78 8Share 文字记录立即在 YouTube、Apple 和 Spotify 上收听和观看。请参阅本页顶部的剧集记录，以及底部的剧集时间戳。

•turbopuffer – 一种可扩展性极强、快速且廉价的混合搜索引擎，建立在对象存储之上，被 Anthropic、Linear、Ramp 等尖端公司使用。许多改用涡轮增压技术的公司将搜索费用削减了 50% 或更多，并且更快地获得结果。一探究竟。另外，请查看我在涡轮增压器之上构建的新的和改进的实用工程师搜索！

• 线性——我们开发人员面临的一大挑战是需要审查的代码量巨大。 Linear Diffs 是一项新功能，用于审查 Linear 内部的 PR，将所有上下文集中在一个地方。它还支持堆叠 PR。一探究竟

• WorkOS – WorkOS 内置Airlock，AI 代理的授权层。它会根据代理的意图+您的规则来评估每个请求，然后允许、拒绝或将其路由给人工。可与 Claude Code、Codex 和 MCP 网关配合使用。了解更多

当生成代码变得便宜而验证它是困难的部分时，软件工程会是什么样子？

在科技界，很少有人比萨提亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 更有资格解决这个热门话题。微软首席执行官的职业生涯始于软件工程师——这在大型科技公司的首席执行官中很少见。 Satya 与我一起讨论 Microsoft 的软件构建发生了怎样的变化，以及这对我们软件工程师意味着什么。

我们从 Microsoft 从 2010 年代中期开始拥抱开源以及从公开构建 VS Code 中汲取的经验教训开始。我问微软是如何从 GitHub Copilot 的早期领先地位发展到必须赶上 Cursor 和 Claude Code 的，以及它揭示了围绕快速改进的模型构建产品的哪些内容。

Satya 还解释了“软件工厂”对他意味着什么、为什么规范和验证变得越来越重要，以及开发 Windows 操作系统等产品的团队如何适应。我们还谈到了微软的自愿退出提议、围绕工程职业的人工智能相关焦虑，并听到纳德拉警告不要从初级招聘放缓中得出长期结论。

我们还探索开放和本地模型，为什么公司需要控制自己的人工智能基础设施，以及如何围绕能力日益增强的代理建立保障措施。 Satya 还为想要在这一变革时期脱颖而出的工程师提供了一些建议，以及他为什么愿意花更多时间进行构建。

我很欣赏萨蒂亚的脚踏实地和深思熟虑，以及他在建议验证与法学硕士相关的任何事情和所有事情方面的务实态度，而不是盲目地信任任何东西或任何人（包括供应商或人工智能模型！）我注意到的 12 个最有趣的要点：

1. 一种新的软件工程形式：团队构建软件工厂来改进他们的工作。 Satya 引用了 Azure 网络团队的例子，该团队管理着 500 多家光纤网络运营商，并且最近构建了一个代理系统来更好地管理电子邮件和流程。现在，他们的运营效率大大提高了。 Satya 认为这是“人工智能转型”的现实：棕地致力于建设软件工厂，以改善团队的运作方式，同时继续日常工作。

2. GitHub Copilot 落后于 Claude Code，因为 IDE 在短短六个月内就淡出了人们的视线。开发工具是微软的 DNA，但它完全没有准备好 Claude Code 放弃 IDE 的概念，转而支持命令行。 Satya 承认 Anthropic 的这一举动让他们措手不及，这让他明白，当发生非线性模型跳跃时，使用该模型的外形尺寸可能会快速变化。他还承认 IDE 在短短六个月的时间里就“消失了”，微软在开发工具领域的据点一直是 IDE 和 VS Code。听起来微软在这里吸取了教训，现在开发工具更加灵活，并且不再拘泥于过去的外形因素。

3.“拥有情报”：避免锁定并将代理视为内部风险。 Satya 警告公司要避免与任何单一模型提供商锁定，确保线束、内存和模型不耦合，以便可以轻松更改。他还认为更多的公司应该考虑使用开放模型来保护其核心知识产权（IP）免遭泄露，并建立私人评估来决定使用和升级到哪些模型。他还表示，模型是智能的，但不可靠，因此最好将它们视为“内部风险”，并构建一个单独的系统来验证代理系统是否按预期工作。

4. 微软押注于“混合智能”。 Satya 质疑为什么我们要依赖云来构建人工智能基础设施，去年的前沿等效模型已经可以在笔记本电脑上运行，而上个季度的前沿等效模型也可以在台式机上运行。他预测“混合智能”的概念将获得关注，即让本地人工智能模型在笔记本电脑和台式机上运行，​​并由模型路由器决定何时使用廉价的、“不计量”的本地模型，以及何时路由到云中功能更强大、更昂贵的模型。微软正在构建基础设施，以通过其 Microsoft AI (MAI) 模型和 Surface Laptop Ultra 系列支持此类路由。

news.title: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
news.title_en: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Because Moonshot AI sees diminishing returns in coding, the Beijing startup is redirecting its Kimi language models toward biology, chemistry, and pharma research. International director Giacomo Ficari said at the Web Summit in Lisbon that science demands smarter AI models than law, finance, or code.

Beijing startup DP Technology is integrating Kimi K3.1 Pro into its research assistant BioMaster. In one test, the AI analyzed gene data from 3,696 mouse pancreatic cells and flagged 100 candidate genes in 90 minutes instead of an estimated four hours of human work.

Fully independent breakthroughs are still a long way off. On TCSExam, a 100-problem theoretical CS benchmark, leading models produced verifiable proofs but couldn't crack any open conjectures alone. US rivals hit similar limits. Anthropic's Claude found an enzyme system in September, but mathematicians criticized OpenAI's claimed math and physics breakthroughs. The pharma industry isn't sold yet either. A June Citi survey of 50 US research leaders found 72 percent already using AI broadly, but only 24 percent expect it to noticeably improve drug development success rates.AdAd

news.article_content_zh:
由于 Moonshot AI 看到编码的回报递减，这家北京初创公司正在将其 Kimi 语言模型转向生物学、化学和制药研究。国际总监 Giacomo Ficari 在里斯本网络峰会上表示，科学需要比法律、金融或代码更智能的人工智能模型。

北京初创公司 DP Technology 正在将 Kimi K3.1 Pro 集成到其研究助手 BioMaster 中。在一项测试中，人工智能分析了 3,696 个小鼠胰腺细胞的基因数据，并在 90 分钟内标记了 100 个候选基因，而不是人类估计需要 4 个小时的工作。

news.title: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back
news.title_en: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back

inline_images.caption: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
inline_images.alt: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Nvidia’s board of directors “isn’t considering” having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC. A source tells the outlet the board “is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back.”

Since Huang’s resignation last week, tech executives, along with current and former Nvidia employees, have called for his reinstatement. An online petition to bring Huang back as CEO has amassed more than 180,000 signatures, including from major figures like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and Replit CEO Amjad Masad.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” for Huang to return to Nvidia. A report from the Financial Times also suggests that Huang floated the idea of returning as CEO with some of his colleagues.

Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO. The company has also hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang’s conduct.

Despite public pressure from figures such as Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney to reinstate Huang, the company has appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and retained Wachtell Lipton to conduct a formal conduct investigation.
news.title_zh: 英伟达董事会否决黄仁勋回归议案
news.summary_zh: 英伟达董事会明确拒绝前首席执行官黄仁勋回归，并聘请Wachtell Lipton律师事务所对其行为展开深入调查
news.article_content_zh:
英伟达董事会“不考虑”让黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官。一位消息人士告诉媒体，董事会“专注于对黄进行调查，而不是讨论让他回来。”

自黄上周辞职以来，科技高管以及英伟达现任和前任员工一直呼吁让他复职。一份要求黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官的网上请愿书已收集了超过 18 万个签名，其中包括 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney)、SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Replit 首席执行官阿姆贾德·马萨德 (Amjad Masad) 等重要人物。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，黄回到英伟达“当然不是一个坏主意”。英国《金融时报》的一篇报道还表明，黄与他的一些同事提出了重新担任首席执行官的想法。

Nvidia 任命其首席财务官 Colette Kress 为临时首席执行官。该公司还聘请了 Wachtell Lipton 来调查黄的行为。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英伟达董事会当前正专注于对前首席执行官黄仁勋的合规调查，并明确表示未考虑其回归议程。尽管现任代理首席执行官柯莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）已接管日常运营，但市场针对黄仁勋回归的呼声高涨，包括埃隆·马斯克及蒂姆·斯威尼等科技领袖均签署请愿书。董事会已聘请律所Wachtell Lipton就黄仁勋在职期间的行为进行专项合规性审查。

news.article_content:
On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world.

These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. news.title: OpenAI announces tools to combat CSAM, including an image classifier and new warning screens to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
news.title_en: OpenAI announces tools to combat CSAM, including an image classifier and new warning screens to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children (Ivan Mehta/TechCrunch)
news.author: TechCrunch
news.article_content:
OpenAI today announced new tools to combat child sexual abuse material (CSAM) amid growing safety concerns around the use of AI tools. These features include a new image classifier to detect CSAM, warnings and temporary blocks to prevent users from creating or accessing content that sexualizes children, a new guideline for developers, and a set of tools for law enforcement.

The company unveiled a new image classifier that can detect CSAM images, including the ones generated by AI. OpenAI is giving select companies access to its classifier through its API at no cost. The tool looks for visual signs of abuse in images not seen before and assigns a score that can give an indicative direction to reviewers about dealing with CSAM.

OpenAI said that it developed this classifier with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), and it is working with Tech Coalition and ROOST to share access to the tool. In its early testing with partners, the AI company found that the classifier flags 48% fewer images while finding the same number of abusive images, reducing the work of reviewers. Plus, images flagged by the classifier are twice as likely to be abusive images.

What’s more, the company is adding new warning screens in ChatGPT to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children. ChatGPT will show an alert to users attempting such prompts, direct users towards specialized support to stop harmful behaviour, and also suspend the account for 24 hours as a warning. The app already blocks CSAM content and requests related to it. It said that repeated offences could lead to the account being removed permanently.

OpenAI noted that it formed the message and guidelines around this behavior with organizations and researchers, including Protect Children, the Lucy Faithfull Foundation, and Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, who independently evaluated a trial of deterrent messages.

The company is also publishing guidelines for developers using OpenAI tools to prevent, detect, and help users report CSAM content. It said that in early testing, the guidelines have helped a number of developers adopt child safety tooling and register to report CSAM to NCMEC. OpenAI is also equipping law enforcement dealing with child safety with AI-powered features like dedicated plugins, investigative tools, and complex data analysis, with access managed by program administrators. It is also providing training to investigators along with a field guide on how to use AI.

OpenAI has had several lawsuits against the company blaming its technology for harming users, especially children. Saftey-focused nonprofit Common Sense Media labeled OpenAI’s tech as “unacceptable risk” for teens. Other AI chatbots — specifically Grok — have been used to create nonconsensual sexualized imagery, including of children.

The AI startup had made changes in the last 12 months to its technology including releasing a safety blueprint, updating content guidelines to bar inappropritate content, retuning its model to prevent them from generating harmful content, and releasing a special version of ChatGPT for teens.

news.article_content_zh:
由于人工智能工具的使用安全问题日益引起人们的关注，OpenAI 今天宣布推出新工具来打击儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM)。这些功能包括用于检测 CSAM 的新图像分类器、用于防止用户创建或访问儿童色情内容的警告和临时阻止、针对开发人员的新指南以及一套执法工具。

该公司推出了一种新的图像分类器，可以检测 CSAM 图像，包括人工智能生成的图像。 OpenAI 允许特定公司通过其 API 免费访问其分类器。该工具会在图像中查找以前未见过的滥用行为的视觉迹象，并给出一个分数，为审稿人处理 CSAM 提供指示性指导。

OpenAI 表示，该分类器是与国家失踪和受虐儿童中心 (NCMEC) 合作开发的，并且正在与 Tech Coalition 和 ROOST 合作，共享该工具的访问权限。在与合作伙伴的早期测试中，这家人工智能公司发现，分类器在发现相同数量的滥用图像的同时，标记的图像减少了 48%，从而减少了审核人员的工作。另外，被分类器标记的图像是滥用图像的可能性是其两倍。

更重要的是，该公司正在 ChatGPT 中添加新的警告屏幕，以防止用户访问使儿童色情的材料。 ChatGPT 将向尝试此类提示的用户显示警报，引导用户寻求专门支持以阻止有害行为，并暂停帐户 24 小时作为警告。该应用程序已阻止 CSAM 内容和与其相关的请求。它表示，屡次违规可能会导致该帐户被永久删除。

OpenAI 指出，它与保护儿童组织、Lucy Faithfull 基金会和塔斯马尼亚大学的 Joel Scanlan 等组织和研究人员一起制定了围绕这种行为的信息和指南，后者独立评估了一项威慑信息试验。

该公司还为使用 OpenAI 工具的开发人员发布了指南，以防止、检测和帮助用户报告 CSAM 内容。它表示，在早期测试中，该指南已帮助许多开发者采用儿童安全工具，并注册向 NCMEC 报告 CSAM。 OpenAI 还为处理儿童安全问题的执法部门配备了人工智能驱动的功能，如专用插件、调查工具和复杂的数据分析，并由程序管理员管理访问权限。它还为调查人员提供培训以及如何使用人工智能的现场指南。

OpenAI 已对该公司提起多起诉讼，指责其技术伤害用户，尤其是儿童。专注于安全的非营利组织 Common Sense Media 将 OpenAI 的技术标记为青少年“不可接受的风险”。其他人工智能聊天机器人——特别是 Grok——已被用来创建未经同意的性图像，包括儿童图像。

这家人工智能初创公司在过去 12 个月中对其技术进行了更改，包括发布安全蓝图、更新内容指南以禁止不当内容、重新调整其模型以防止生成有害内容，以及为青少年发布特殊版本的 ChatGPT。

news.title: Sources: Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO and is focused on a national security investigation into Huang (CNBC)
news.title_en: Sources: Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO and is focused on a national security investigation into Huang (CNBC)

inline_images.caption: Nvidia board not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC
inline_images.alt: Nvidia board not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC

news.author: CNBC
news.article_content:
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.

The board is focused on a national security investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, the person said.

Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company he founded, after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came under a week after Huang had admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had an affair with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer, as well as employees at Nvidia.

Over the weekend, the Financial Times said Huang had discussed coming back with allies. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on speculation on Sunday.

Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO.

An online petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn 180,000 signatures as well as support from major figures including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

On Friday, a representative for Nvidia's board said that it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role.

news.title: Anthropic cuts its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, in response to AI-driven bug discovery (Anthropic)
news.title_en: Anthropic cuts its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, in response to AI-driven bug discovery (Anthropic)

inline_images.caption: Two-panel illustration: on the left, a black-and-white photograph of a large boulder, tinted yellow, balanced on smaller rocks; on the right, a blue line drawin
inline_images.alt: Two-panel illustration: on the left, a black-and-white photograph of a large boulder, tinted yellow,

news.author: Anthropic
news.article_content:
Over the last several months, frontier models have become much better at discovering vulnerabilities. We remain optimistic that this will help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities faster than ever before. However, the speed at which AI is improving has changed how we think about our own disclosure practices.

We’re shortening the disclosure window in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported to vendors and maintainers on or after January 1, 2027. In-progress reports as of that date will keep their existing deadlines.

In addition to shortening the disclosure window, we are making two related changes. First, we will aim to escalate to an external vulnerability coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 if a maintainer does not respond to our initial vulnerability report. Second, we will wait 30 days instead of 45 after a patch is available before sharing full technical details. The rest of our policy remains the same.

Finally, there are high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities that we reported over 90 days ago and that now exceed the deadline in our current CVD policy that have not yet been disclosed publicly. We are now notifying the maintainers of these projects that we are providing them an additional 30 days, after which time we will publish these reports on our dashboard in line with our updated policy starting January 1, 2027.

Many coordinated disclosure norms, including those found in our own policy, were developed well before AI could discover vulnerabilities. These policies assumed that fixes moved at human speed and that independent rediscovery of the same bug was unlikely. Neither assumption holds today. Models can now help develop fixes, and a bug that one model can find is increasingly likely to be found by another. We are seeing a higher rate of vulnerability rediscovery as these capabilities increase. A 90-day window made sense when a vulnerability could be expected to stay private for months. We no longer believe it can, and these changes are intended to keep pace with progress in AI capabilities and strike the right balance for defenders.

Some vulnerabilities still can’t be fixed quickly. Flaws in hard-to-deploy software, such as critical infrastructure, and flaws that require changes to a specification or RFC can’t always be resolved in 30 or 45 days. In these cases, we will work with the vendor on a remediation timeline. Our seven-day disclosure window for any vulnerability under active exploitation remains unchanged. This new policy update will not apply to AI-discovered findings that have not received human review, such as those found by OSS Scanner.

We recognize that shorter timelines may put more pressure on software maintainers. To reduce that burden, we will continue to include actionable guidance with each report, along with a patch or mitigation where possible, to best enable the maintainer to confirm a finding and fix the vulnerability. We will also continue to agree on a sustainable pace with maintainers before sending a large volume of findings to a single project.

news.article_content_zh:
在过去的几个月里，前沿模型在发现漏洞方面变得更加出色。我们仍然乐观地认为，这将帮助防御者比以往更快地发现和修复漏洞。然而，人工智能改进的速度改变了我们对自己的披露实践的看法。

我们将协调漏洞披露 (CVD) 政策中的披露窗口从 90 天缩短到 30 天（对于高严重性和关键严重性问题），对于所有其他问题则从 45 天缩短。新的时间表适用于 2027 年 1 月 1 日或之后向供应商和维护人员报告的漏洞。截至该日期正在进行的报告将保留现有的截止日期。

除了缩短披露窗口外，我们还进行了两项相关的更改。首先，如果维护人员未对我们的初始漏洞报告做出回应，我们的目标是在 15 天（而不是 30 天）后将问题升级给外部漏洞协调员。其次，我们将在补丁发布后等待 30 天而不是 45 天，然后再分享完整的技术细节。我们政策的其余部分保持不变。

最后，我们在 90 多天前报告了一些高危和危急严重的漏洞，这些漏洞现在已经超过了我们当前 CVD 政策的截止日期，但尚未公开披露。我们现在通知这些项目的维护者，我们将为他们提供额外的 30 天时间，之后我们将根据自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起更新的政策在我们的仪表板上发布这些报告。

许多协调一致的披露规范，包括我们自己政策中的规范，都是在人工智能发现漏洞之前就制定的。这些政策假设修复工作以人类的速度进行，并且独立地重新发现相同的错误是不可能的。这两种假设在今天都不成立。模型现在可以帮助开发修复程序，并且一个模型可以找到的错误越来越有可能被另一个模型发现。随着这些功能的增强，我们发现漏洞重新发现率更高。当漏洞预计会在数月内保持私密状态时，90 天的窗口是有意义的。我们不再相信它可以，这些变化旨在跟上人工智能能力的进步，并为防御者取得适当的平衡。

一些漏洞仍然无法快速修复。难以部署的软件（例如关键基础设施）中的缺陷以及需要更改规范或 RFC 的缺陷并不总能在 30 或 45 天内得到解决。在这些情况下，我们将与供应商合作制定补救时间表。我们对任何被主动利用的漏洞的 7 天披露窗口保持不变。此新政策更新不适用于人工智能发现的未经人工审核的结果，例如 OSS Scanner 发现的结果。

我们认识到，较短的时间可能会给软件维护人员带来更大的压力。为了减轻这种负担，我们将继续在每份报告中提供可操作的指导，并在可能的情况下提供补丁或缓解措施，以最好地使维护人员能够确认发现并修复漏洞。在向单个项目发送大量调查结果之前，我们还将继续与维护人员就可持续的步伐达成一致。

我们提供计划来帮助维护者和防御者以这种新的节奏工作。关键开源项目的维护者可以申请 OSS Scanner，这是一项免费服务，可以使用我们最强大的模型定期扫描他们的代码，并直接向他们发送结果。符合条件的维护者和贡献者可以向 Claude 开源计划免费申请六个月的 Claude Ultra。安全专业人员，包括开源维护人员，可以申请我们的网络验证计划，该计划定制克劳德的保护措施以实现合法的防御工作。

news.author: OpenAI 官方动态
news.article_content:
We’re expanding the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to give up to 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to ChatGPT.

The program began as a pilot in July. Applications for the next round open Monday, November 23. We’ll award 50,000 new grants to eligible researchers on a first-come, first-served basis. Each grant gives the recipient and up to two collaborators free access to ChatGPT Plus. If you’re already on the waitlist and qualify, we’ll email you before applications open with instructions for activating your account.

Participants can use OpenAI’s frontier models and get training on how to use ChatGPT in their research. By default, we don’t use data shared through the program to train our models.

Waitlist signups by country or territory as of November 12, 2026. Darker colors indicate more signups on a logarithmic scale.

20,000 researchers in 33 countries have joined the program since the pilot began in July. Shuqi Li, a researcher at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Harvard Medical School, looks for new drug targets that could ultimately shorten tuberculosis treatment. He is exploring whether ChatGPT can help link lab and patient data to speed up antibiotic development. Arthur Porto, assistant curator of AI biodiversity at the Florida Museum of Natural History, and his team uses AI tools to turn photographs of museum specimens into searchable databases. They also created a 3D model of a butterfly whose wings change color as you turn it, just like the real specimen.

We’re also publishing Science at the Frontier: How Scientists Use ChatGPT, new research from our Economic Research team examining how more than 1,800 researchers used ChatGPT during the program’s summer pilot. Surveyed participants estimated that, without AI, the same research work at the same quality would have taken nearly twice as long.

The program’s summer pilot helped us understand how researchers use ChatGPT and how we can improve their experience. Based on feedback from researchers, we’re moving away from lottery-based selection. For the next round, we’ll provide access to the first 50,000 applications who meet the eligibility requirements.

The pilot gave researchers access to ChatGPT Pro. When we reviewed pilot usage, we found that most participants would have stayed within ChatGPT Plus usage limits. Based on that finding, we’re offering Plus for new grants so we can extend access to more research teams.

Each grant for this round covers the recipient and up to two collaborators, supporting up to 150,000 researchers. Our goal for the program as a whole is to reach 200,000 researchers, double the goal we announced when the pilot launched in July.

We’ll continue learning from participants about the application process, the capabilities they need, and the support that helps them use these tools in their research. This feedback will help us refine the program and shape future rounds.

Different scientific fields will use AI in different ways, and researchers will need different kinds and levels of support. We’re working with scientific communities to understand those needs and shape our tools, training, and programs around them.

Our support also includes helping scientific communities turn AI-generated results into deeper understanding and new discoveries. In mathematics, we contributed $5 million to a new Simons Foundation initiative⁠ to help mathematicians examine, understand, and build on results produced by AI.

news.article_content_zh:
我们正在扩大针对学术研究人员的 ChatGPT 计划，让全球多达 200,000 名研究人员免费访问 ChatGPT。

该计划于七月开始试点。下一轮申请将于 11 月 23 日星期一开放。我们将按照先到先得的原则向符合条件的研究人员提供 50,000 笔新资助。每笔资助都会让接受者和最多两名合作者免费访问 ChatGPT Plus。如果您已经在候补名单上并且符合资格，我们会在申请开放之前向您发送电子邮件，其中包含激活您帐户的说明。

参与者可以使用 OpenAI 的前沿模型，并接受如何在研究中使用 ChatGPT 的培训。默认情况下，我们不使用通过程序共享的数据来训练我们的模型。

截至 2026 年 11 月 12 日，按国家或地区列出的候补名单注册人数。较深的颜色表示对数标度上的注册人数较多。

自 7 月份试点开始以来，已有 33 个国家的 20,000 名研究人员加入了该计划。布莱根妇女医院和哈佛医学院的研究员 Shuqi Li 正在寻找最终可以缩短结核病治疗时间的新药物靶点。他正在探索 ChatGPT 是否可以帮助连接实验室和患者数据，以加快抗生素的开发。佛罗里达自然历史博物馆人工智能生物多样性助理馆长 Arthur Porto 和他的团队使用人工智能工具将博物馆标本的照片转化为可搜索的数据库。他们还创建了蝴蝶的 3D 模型，其翅膀会随着转动而改变颜色，就像真实的标本一样。

我们还发布了《科学前沿：科学家如何使用 ChatGPT》，这是我们经济研究团队的新研究，研究了 1,800 多名研究人员在该项目夏季试点期间如何使用 ChatGPT。接受调查的参与者估计，如果没有人工智能，相同质量的相同研究工作将花费近两倍的时间。

我们希望更多的研究人员拥有工具和支持来追求雄心勃勃的问题并做出改善人们生活的发现。这是我们确保通用人工智能造福全人类的使命的核心。

该计划的夏季试点帮助我们了解研究人员如何使用 ChatGPT 以及我们如何改善他们的体验。根据研究人员的反馈，我们正在放弃基于抽签的选择。在下一轮中，我们将向前 50,000 名符合资格要求的申请提供访问权限。

该试点项目让研究人员能够访问 ChatGPT Pro。当我们审查试点使用情况时，我们发现大多数参与者都会遵守 ChatGPT Plus 使用限制。基于这一发现，我们将向 Plus 提供新的资助，以便我们可以将访问范围扩大到更多的研究团队。

此轮的每笔资助涵盖接受者和最多两名合作者，支持多达 150,000 名研究人员。我们整个计划的目标是覆盖 200,000 名研究人员，是我们 7 月份试点启动时宣布的目标的两倍。

我们将继续向参与者了解申请流程、他们所需的功能以及帮助他们在研究中使用这些工具的支持。这些反馈将帮助我们完善计划并塑造未来的轮次。

不同的科学领域会以不同的方式使用人工智能，研究人员需要不同种类和水平的支持。我们正在与科学界合作，了解这些需求，并围绕它们制定我们的工具、培训和计划。

我们的支持还包括帮助科学界将人工智能生成的结果转化为更深入的理解和新发现。在数学方面，我们向西蒙斯基金会的一项新计划捐赠了 500 万美元，以帮助数学家检查、理解人工智能产生的结果并在其基础上进行构建。

我们还为研究人员和机构提供不同的方式来访问我们的工具。面向学术研究人员的 ChatGPT 只是我们帮助研究人员访问先进人工智能工具的一种方式。
